The driver had a traffic reason on the record: the Ayer Rajah Expressway, part of the recommended corridor, was at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h, congestion) throughout 18:25–18:59, covering the whole period of the off-route segment, with no other incident recorded nearby.

Under RD-1/RD-2 the refundable amount is the excess distance fare only, which the fare record states as $7.81 (5.54 km × $1.4099/km this trip's distance rate); time fare, platform fee and any surge are not refunded, and surge here was 1.0× so no surge differential can be added on top.

Because the record is complete — timestamped chat, continuous GPS with a segmented track, and traffic data — the case is decidable and needs no escalation under TH-4; the disputed amount ($7.81) is under $10, so under TH-1/TH-2 the system ruling is final and follows the DISP-001 route-deviation precedent.

No driver violation should be recorded under RD-2/RD-6: this segment is excused by rider consent and a traffic reason, and the driver's 90-day record shows 0 upheld route deviations, so no flag_account is warranted.

weaknesses: The off-route segment is large and not marginal — 4.97 km added, up to 1384 m from the optimal route, 7.35 km where the optimal route covers 2.38 km (F3), which the rider will use to show the 'another way' was a long detour rather than an alternative.

The rider's 18:46 message bars a specific road ('不要走 Clementi Avenue 2', F8); the rider will argue the reply was a narrow, conditional permission — one road out, everything else unchanged — not a general route consent, and that a driver who hears a condition should stay close to the corridor.

The traffic justification is thin at the roadside: F11 shows AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY at band 2 during 18:25–18:59, but there is no traffic incident near the route (F14), the recommended route also uses the CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY at band 7 (60–69 km/h) (F12), and the segment instead drove a 7.35 km loop through Clementi, Kent Ridge and Pasir Panjang (F3) — the rider will say nothing on the record shows a closure, incident or congestion on the replaced part of the recommended route at trip time (RD-4).

The driver's post-trip statement (F10) that he 'kept off one road' is a claim about his own conduct, not rider consent, and under RD-5 a driver's word alone does not carry the consent element; the consent argument rests entirely on F8.

The whole trip overran the recommended distance by more than the single segment (F1: +5.6 km vs the segment's +4.97 km, F3), so the rider can argue part of the excess sits outside any consented segment, and the billed excess (F4) exceeds what one segment accounts for.

TH-2 notes DISP-001 resolved a 4.3 km deviation to a $3.44 partial refund automatically; the rider will press for the full excess distance fare of $7.81 (F4), and the trip's metered total of $57.35 (F6) sits well above the estimate, which colours the judge's reading of 'a long way round'.

points.response: Accepted as far as it goes: F1 and F3 establish +5.6 km overall and a single 4.97 km off-route segment, over RD-1's 1 km tolerance, so RD-2 applies — but the consequence the driver draws (no refund) does not follow, because neither exemption in RD-2's matrix is made out on this record.

Notice is not the disputed element — the notice requirement in RD-5 is satisfied by F7 sent at 18:45 before the 18:48 segment; what is missing is the rider's agreement to the route actually driven, because F8 consented only to 'another way' with one road barred.

Conceded only in part: F8 does leave the general route to the driver and does honour the exclusion of Clementi Avenue 2 (not among the F3 roads driven), so this segment is general route consent, but general consent cannot exempt the excess distance under RD-2 — the refundable km are the excess minus only segments exempt under RD-3 or RD-5, and a driver who runs 7.35 km where 2.38 km suffices, up to 1384 m off the optimal route through Kent Ridge and Pasir Panjang, exceeds anything F8 authorised.

The driver is right that only a road to be avoided was named in F8, which is exactly why F8 is general route consent and not an agreement to any named route; but RD-5's system detail then puts the burden on the driver to show the route was within the general permission, and a 4.97 km loop that reached nothing the rider asked for is not.

F11 shows only the Ayer Rajah Expressway at band 2 — congestion, not an incident or closure — and F14 records no traffic incident near the route, while the segment in F3 left the corridor altogether for a 7.35 km loop through Clementi, Kent Ridge, Pasir Panjang and South Buona Vista; RD-4 needs a traffic event on the replaced part of the recommended route or a 1–2 speed band there, and under RD-4 a traffic reason at most excuses the driver's violation — it does not exempt the segment from the refund (RD-2 row 2: rider informed, but here the reroute's extent was never agreed, so the excess is still refunded).
Agreed on the calculation: the refundable figure is $7.81 (5.54 km × $1.4099/km) per F4, time fare, platform fee and the 1.0× surge (F5, F6) are excluded, and the rider asks for exactly that.

The rider does not seek escalation; the record is complete (F9: two timestamped messages) and the disputed amount of $7.81 is under $10, so the system rules under TH-1/TH-2 consistently with the DISP-001 partial-refund precedent.

A violation is recorded only where the deviation has no traffic reason; even accepting F11's band-2 congestion as a reason, RD-2 still refunds the excess distance fare because the rider was told a jam existed but never agreed to a 4.97 km detour, so the refund stands whether or not the violation is logged, and the rider presses flag_account only if the segment is found unjustified.
Withdrawn as a request: the rider does not ask for flag_account, since F17 shows 0 upheld route deviations in the driver's 90-day history, and the refund does not depend on it.

Conceded on the arithmetic: the deviation is +5.6 km over the 1 km tolerance (F1, F2), so RD-1/RD-2 are engaged — but that only opens the exemption analysis, not the outcome, since exempt km under RD-3/RD-5 are deducted before any refund is computed (RD-2, RD-1).

Accepted that the segment is real driving and not map-matching noise: 7.35 km against 2.38 km optimal, +4.97 km, up to 1384 m off route (F3). That is precisely why the segment's ground matters — if it is consent-exempt under RD-5 the km come out of the refundable total, and the segment far exceeds RD-1's 0.2 km noise threshold either way.

This point argues both ways: the rider agrees the message was a general route choice, and a general route choice before the segment is exactly RD-5 consent ('a brief reason is enough; acknowledged → agreed'), not a signature on each road; the rider's reply '可以' authorises the alternative way the driver proposed at 18:45, and the segment began at 18:48, after that exchange (F7, F8, F3).

The rider's own reading confirms the one express condition was honoured — Clementi Avenue 2 appears nowhere in the roads driven (F3, F8) — and RD-5's road-name check only bites where a rider agreed to 'go via X'; here the only road named was named to be avoided, so there is no road the segment had to have taken.

I do not rely on the driver's statement for consent; the consent element rests on the rider's own timestamped message at 18:46 (F8), which RD-5 §1.2 makes the controlling record, and the statement in F10 is offered only as corroboration that the exclusion was kept.

RD-4 is satisfied on the record: the Ayer Rajah Expressway is on the recommended corridor at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) throughout 18:25–18:59, covering the entire off-route segment 18:48–18:59 (F11, F3), and RD-4's band criterion is a 'traffic reason' without requiring that the congestion sit on the exact roads replaced; the absence of incidents (F14, F15) and the expressway's own band 7 stretch (F12) go to degree, not to the existence of a traffic reason.

The $7.81 figure is not in dispute as the arithmetic of excess distance (F4, F5, F6); what is in dispute is how much of it survives RD-2's exemption step, and because consent plus a traffic reason are in the record the outcome row is 'no_action' with no driver violation — at the lowest, only the excess distance fare falls within any refund, and no time, platform or surge element does (F5, F6).

The rider's inference is unfounded: the profile shows 0 upheld route deviations in 90 days (F17), the 1 upheld dispute is not a route case, and RD-6 needs an upheld deviation in this case before any flag could attach — so no flag_account is available to the rider here.

The rider's clean profile (F16) is not contested and decides nothing: RD-6 and TH-3 both say profile facts can never be the finding, so 0 upheld disputes neither proves the route was agreed nor disproves the driver's consent and traffic evidence (F8, F11).
